clue.text: Escape for holiday abroad

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
out of the country, as in 'out in France'

explanation.surface: Someone longs to get away and treats a trip overseas as a means of escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakout is a jailbreak, a successful escape from prison or confinement.

clue.text: Writer eating only half of stew in restaurant

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the following letters go into the writer

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writing instrument

indicators.note: only half survives, so the second half of the word is thrown away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An author eats a small portion of stew at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author but is a pen; Biro is the British trade name for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant serving simple food.

clue.text: Star anise, say, always growing

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'for ever'
green describes growing, unripe vegetation

explanation.surface: Star anise is described as an ever-thriving plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Star anise comes from an evergreen tree that keeps its leaves all year, so it is an example.

clue.text: Reportedly drops off a novel

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by voice, so we go by sound and not spelling

parts.note: to kip is to sleep, so someone who drops off kips

explanation.surface: Someone is said to doze off over a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipps is an H. G. Wells novel of 1905; kip is British slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipps is the title of a comic novel by H. G. Wells about a draper's assistant.

clue.text: Drunk carried out secretly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: so intoxicated as to have slid off one's chair
second meaning: done covertly, as with a bribe passed out of sight

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a drunk being carried home quietly; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes both someone who has collapsed from drinking and an illicit deal done covertly.

clue.text: Stretch of lake twists to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: L is the standard map abbreviation for lake
to warp is to twist out of shape

explanation.surface: A length of lakeside winds westward.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprawl is to stretch out one's limbs lazily, so the verb sense matches.

clue.text: Clerical worker in dock, drug dealer

parts.note: a pen is a sheltered dock, as a submarine pen
a pusher sells illegal drugs

explanation.surface: An office clerk stands in the dock charged as a drug dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' suggests the court, but here it is a berth for vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a disparaging term for an office worker doing routine paperwork.

clue.text: A bit to one side

parts.note: taken as written
a part is a bit or portion

explanation.surface: Something is placed slightly off to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means aside or separated, as in setting something apart from the rest.

clue.text: Able to read and write Latin? Say again

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Latin
to iterate is to repeat or restate

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a reading and writing qualification extends to Latin, and requests a repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Literate is the standard word for a person with the skills of reading and writing.

clue.text: Lottery could cause son to shed tears

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to weep is to cry

explanation.surface: A lottery loss might leave a boy in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep is short for sweepstake, a draw in which entrants win the pooled stakes.

clue.text: Support worker accused

parts.note: to defend is to back or support
the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker

explanation.surface: Backing a colleague who stands accused of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: The defendant is the person accused and on trial in a court case.

clue.text: Chinese restaurant speciality? Chef brought in fourteen I fancy!

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside, so one piece goes into the other
to fancy something is to imagine it, so the letters take an imagined new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: A diner fancies fourteen dishes from a chef at a Chinese restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: COOK goes inside the rearranged letters, after the first seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune cookies, holding a printed prediction, are served after meals in Chinese restaurants in the West.

clue.text: Hospital doctor injecting substance right into bottom

indicators.note: to inject is to push something inside, so these letters go in
into says where the injected letters end up: within the following word

parts.note: the rear is the backside
the gist is the substance or essence of something
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A doctor gives an injection in the buttock, the usual site for a jab.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a registrar is a grade of doctor, not the official who records births and marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a senior trainee doctor ranked below a consultant.

clue.text: Total, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: complete or absolute, as an adjective
second meaning: to speak or voice, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual 'for example' marker, but it is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning absolute (utter nonsense) and a verb meaning to speak words aloud.

clue.text: Considered striking after spring, so planned carefully

indicators.note: after tells us the preceding words come second in the line, behind the word that follows

parts.note: a spring is a natural well
considered means thought about
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A strike called after spring was considered and carefully planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-thought-out has been devised with care and attention to every detail.

clue.text: Fine sight, a kaleidoscopic display

parts.note: light means fine or delicate, as in a light touch
a show is a sight or spectacle

explanation.surface: A beautiful spectacle full of shifting colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A light show is a display of coloured, moving lights, often accompanying music.

clue.text: Title of new wine shop across river

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so the letters go around
new suggests a fresh version, so the following letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: The deeds to a new wine shop on the far side of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, title is the right of ownership of property.

clue.text: Film barmaids working

indicators.note: working suggests being worked on or kneaded, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A movie about women working behind a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's Rib is a 1949 courtroom comedy film starring Spencer Tracy and Katharine Hepburn.

clue.text: Need MOT? GT somehow not right, please understand

indicators.note: somehow says the letters get there by some unstated means, so they are reshuffled

parts.note: taken letter for letter
something not right is wrong

explanation.surface: A sports car owner pleads that the vehicle needs its annual roadworthiness test because something is not right.
explanation.walkthrough: An MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars; a GT is a grand tourer, a fast touring car.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to head off a misunderstanding, asking the listener to grasp one's real meaning.

clue.text: Thin daughter did without

parts.note: spare can mean lean or thin, of a figure
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A slim daughter skipped a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare something is to manage without it, as in 'could you spare it?'

clue.text: Fighter plane hit? One's lost power

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

indicators.note: something that has been lost is no longer there, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A fighter jet is struck and loses engine power.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or force, a close synonym of power.

clue.text: Drawn, relative after onset of gout

indicators.note: the onset is the very start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative looks haggard as gout begins to set in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the relative behind the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn and gaunt both describe a face looking thin, haggard and tired.

clue.text: Diver with net revealing explosive device

parts.note: the booby is a seabird that dives for fish
a net is a kind of trap

explanation.surface: A scuba diver's net turns out to hide a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' suggests a person underwater; here it is a diving seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby trap is a hidden bomb set to go off when an unsuspecting person touches it.

clue.text: Long story about Egypt's leader

indicators.note: about means around, so the story wraps the other letter

parts.note: a yarn is a tall tale

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale concerning the ruler of Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the story; it is the verb meaning to crave.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it, both verbs of deep wanting.

clue.text: Thug's hairy pet

parts.note: rough can mean shaggy or hairy, as of a coat
to pet is to kiss and cuddle, also called necking

explanation.surface: A tough guy owns a shaggy dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like an animal, but it is the verb for kissing and cuddling.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughneck is a rowdy, uncouth man, often a hired heavy, so a thug.

clue.text: Actress in part of Dumas heroine

indicators.note: a part of the following words contains what we want, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An actress plays a role as a heroine of Alexandre Dumas.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Asher is an English actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Asher is a well-known British actress of stage and screen, so the surname stands for her.

clue.text: Former name of Ottawa, according to name on tug

indicators.note: placed on means coming after, so the second word follows the first

parts.note: by means according to, as in 'by the book'
to tug a vessel is to tow it
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A town name painted on a tugboat says where it is from.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa was known as Bytown, after Colonel John By, before its renaming in 1855.

clue.text: Girl's back at school to get a laxative

indicators.note: back says the name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name; with the possessive it reads Anne's
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A girl returns to school and is given a laxative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' suggests a classroom, but it is a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna pods, the dried fruit of the senna plant, are a traditional purgative remedy.
